"'''Calm Down'''" is a song by Nigerian singer [[Rema (musician)|Rema]], from his debut studio album ''[[Rave & Roses]]'' (2022). It was released on 11 February 2022 through [[Jonzing World]], [[Mavin Records|Mavin]], and [[Interscope Records]] as the album's second single. The song charted across Europe, reaching number one on the Belgian [[Ultratop 50]], [[Dutch Top 40]] and [[Dutch Single Top 100]]. In the United Kingdom, "Calm Down" peaked at number three on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and spent 27 non-consecutive weeks in the top ten of the chart.

A remix of "Calm Down" with American singer [[Selena Gomez]] was released on 25 August 2022. The new version reached number one on both the [[Billboard U.S. Afrobeats Songs|''Billboard'' US Afrobeats]] Songs and the [[Billboard Global Excl. US|''Billboard'' Global Excl. US]] charts, and peaked at number three on the [[Billboard Global 200|Global 200]] chart. It peaked at number three on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], marking Rema's first top-ten hit and Gomez's ninth. It also led the U.S. [[Billboard U.S. Afrobeats Songs|Afrobeats Songs]] for a record-setting 58 weeks. In the US, it topped the all-genre [[Radio Songs (chart)|Radio Songs]] chart for ten weeks, becoming both artists' first number-one song on the chart. It reached number one on the [[Canadian Hot 100]] chart dated 13 May 2023. According to the [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]] (IFPI), the remix was the second best-selling global single of 2023, earning 1.89 billion subscription streams equivalents globally. Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Naming the song one of the best of 2022, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' said "Rema likes to call his spin on the [[Afrobeats]] sound "Afro-rave," and it is sublimely lovely all the same. He is the kind of singer who savors simple pop pleasures; with a track that's appropriately warm, bright, and captivating. The big-eyed wonder in his voice makes it sound like he's the first guy ever to behold the majesty of girls or colors."<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 December 2023 |title=The 100 Best Songs of 2022 |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-songs-2022-list-1234632381/bad-bunny-titi-me-pregunto-1234632382/ |access-date=8 December 2023 |magazine=RollingStone}}</ref> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' said the song is organic, and its slow burn is further underscoring Afrobeats' increasing mainstream popularity, while naming it the 10th best song of 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 December 2023 |title=The 100 Best Songs of 2023: Staff Picks |url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/best-songs-2023/ |access-date=8 December 2023 |magazine=Billboard}}</ref>
